context: Answered Oct 28 02:43 CDT, (a): a Mac session finds which GitHub connection fails and whether its token expired, changing nothing; the fix follows from the cause. Brief: briefs/c87-mac-github-token-check.md on the roadmap branch. A clue it carries: in the cloud the GitHub plugin fails with "Authorization header is badly formatted" while gh works.

options.gain: You learn whether a token expired before anything changes.
options.how: A local session lists every GitHub connection on the Mac, checks each token (gh auth status, expiry), and reports which one fails and why; it changes nothing.
options.label: A Mac session finds the cause
options.lose: Needs a Mac session for a few minutes.

options.gain: Fixes it fast if the token is the cause.
options.how: You create a new fine-grained token and a Mac session puts it where the failing piece reads it.
options.label: Make a fresh token now
options.lose: If the token is not the cause, it fixes nothing.

options.how: Remove the failing GitHub connection from the Mac and Windows.
options.label: Turn it off on both machines
options.lose: No GitHub plugin locally; sessions use the gh CLI only.

ref: c87 (local sessions stop failing on the GitHub plugin's empty token)
title: The GitHub plugin fails on the Mac too: find out why first?
why: It answers your token question without changing anything, and the fix then follows from the cause.
